judgment.rationale: Both Indicators sit in BASIC 4, Strand 3 Geometry and Measurement, Sub-Strand 3 Measurement (Perimeter and Area), and both turn on the shared skill of using measurement referents (LC tags/text share 'referents'). The first (B4.3.3.1.1, under the perimeter Content Standard) asks pupils to estimate perimeter using referents for the linear units centimetre or metre; the second (B4.3.3.2.2, under the area Content Standard 'Demonstrate an understanding of area of regular and irregular 2-D shapes') asks them to select and justify referents for the square units cm² or m², with LCs splitting into 'select referents' and 'justify referents'. This is a substantive extension rather than repetition: familiarity with personal/linear referents for cm and m supports the more demanding task of choosing and justifying referents for the derived square units and involves added justification reasoning, so same-rank forward direction from the linear-referent estimation skill to the square-unit referent selection/justification is supported. Endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context (including the B4.3.3.1 code-collision boundary note for the perimeter branch) and truncated source evidence, which limits but does not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 6 Indicators (same grain, same rank 2) under Strand 1: Number / Sub-Strand 2: Number Operations. The first (B6.1.2.1.1) develops mental-mathematics strategies and number properties to determine basic multiplication facts to 81 and the related division facts, with LCs on skip counting, doubling/halving, repeated doubling/halving and 9s/11s patterns. The second (B6.1.2.4.1, under Content Standard B6.1.2.4 on division of 2- or 3-digit numbers by 1- or 2-digit numbers) requires dividing 3-digit numbers by a 1-digit number 'efficiently'. Recall and flexible use of basic division facts is the substantive underpinning of efficient multi-digit division procedures, so proficiency in the first supports success in the second; the change is from single-fact recall/mental strategy to applying it within multi-digit division. Same-rank direction rests on this pair-specific content dependency, not on code prefix or shared ancestors alone (the nomination's lexical overlap evidence is weak: shared tokens 'division'/'number' only). Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated, limiting exemplar detail.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Indicators (B5.1.1.2.2 at BASIC 5, rank 1; B6.1.1.2.2 at BASIC 6, rank 2) under identically worded Content Standards ('Demonstrate understanding of Roman Numerals up to C (i.e. 100)') in the Number strand. Their statement text is word-for-word identical ('Count and convert Hindu Arabic numbers to Roman numerals up to 100 (C) and vice versa'), and they share all three Learning Components with identical skill scope (count to 100 (C); convert Hindu Arabic to Roman; convert Roman to Hindu Arabic). Upstream merge notes confirm these are distinct grade-scoped items rather than a duplicate, so the pair represents genuine cross-grade recurrence of the same conversion skill at the same numeric ceiling. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicators of the same grain under Content Standard B4.1.1.3 ('Demonstrate an understanding of factors, multiples and squared numbers'), Sub-Strand Counting, Representation & Cardinality, Strand NUMBER, at the same resolved BASIC 4 coordinate (rank 0). Beyond shared placement, the statement texts and Learning Components show a pair-specific progression: B4.1.1.3.1 asks learners to generate the complete set of factors of a single given number up to 50 (systematic divisibility listing for one number), whereas B4.1.1.3.3 requires determining the lowest common multiple of at least two given numbers up to 100 — a larger number range, two or more numbers at once, and comparison/selection across generated lists. Fluency with systematically generating and exhausting divisor/multiple lists for one number plausibly supports success on the two-number LCM task, so the developmental direction runs second_to_first; the same-rank direction rests on this substantive increase in number of operands, range, and comparison demand rather than on the code prefix or page proximity, which are weak signals only. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (32 and 24 omitted source-evidence items), so exemplar detail that could refine the LCM/factor link is not visible, and the parent Content Standard and the LCM Indicator carry upstream merge context (duplicate-occurrence merges) that was inspected and found not to alter the statement wording or scope.

judgment.rationale: Both are Indicators at the same BASIC 4 rank in Strand 2: Algebra, Sub-strand 1: Patterns and Relationships, so direction rests on statement content rather than coordinate. B4.2.1.1.2 ('Determine the missing element(s) in a given table or chart') sits under Content Standard B4.2.1.1, which targets identifying and describing patterns found in tables and charts; filling a missing element requires recognising the underlying pattern in a single table or chart. B4.2.1.3.2 ('Identify and extend the patterns in a table or chart to solve a given problem'), under Content Standard B4.2.1.3 ('Represent, describe and extend patterns and relationships, using charts and tables, to solve problems'), takes that same table/chart pattern reading and extends it beyond the given entries and applies it to a stated problem — a substantive increase in complexity (extension plus problem application). Proficiency in determining missing elements therefore supports success in identifying and extending patterns to solve problems, so the developmental direction is second_to_first. Shared LC tokens ('patterns', 'table', 'chart') and the common code prefix are corroborating, not decisive, evidence; both endpoints carry truncated source evidence and upstream audit/merge context, which limits certainty on the full exemplar detail.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Content Standards in Strand 1: Number at the same canonical rank (2), but in different Sub-Strands: B6.1.4.1 (Ratios and Proportion) asks for understanding of the concept of ratios and its relationship to fractions and to the multiplication and division of whole numbers, while B6.1.2.2 (Number Operations) targets understanding multiplication of a 2 or 3-digit number by a 2 or 3-digit number. The ratio standard explicitly invokes whole-number multiplication/division, so there is genuine multiplicative-reasoning coherence beyond the shared parent, shared code prefix and generic 'demonstrate understanding of multiplication' wording that triggered nomination. However, B6.1.2.2 is a computational extension to larger multi-digit factors rather than the conceptual multiplicative structure ratios draw on, and with a same-rank gap of 0 and no Learning Components supplied there is no substantive evidence to assert a developmental direction either way; symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment.
